If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to hedge downside risk.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to mid-horizon (8–15 days) to align with momentum bias.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from mid-horizon (8–15 days) to avoid overcorrection.

In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is positive, apply +0.3–0.7% to forecast to reflect sustained bullishness; if negative, apply -0.3–0.7% to reflect fading momentum.

If sentiment swings from negative to positive within 3 days, adjust forecast at 10-day mark by +1.0–1.5% to capture reversal momentum.
